record.paper_title: The Critical Beta-splitting Random Tree II: Overview and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Transfer of CLTs from fringe process to finite trees
record.original_question: Let (T_i, i in Z) denote the stationary fringe process obtained from the local weak fringe-tree limit, and let T_i^(n) denote DTCS(n) re-rooted at leaf i. If a given functional Φ satisfies a central limit theorem for the fringe-process sums Σ_{i=0}^{m-1} Φ(T_i), determine whether the analogous central limit theorem must also hold for the finite-tree sums Σ_{i=1}^n Φ(T_i^(n)) in DTCS(n).

evidence.quote: By re-rooting a realization of the fringe tree at leaf i, we get a stationary random process (Ti, −∞ < i < ∞) taking values in the tree-space.
Open Problem 12 If we know that, for a given functional Φ, a CLT holds for the fringe process Pm−1_i=0 Φ(Ti), does the same CLT necessarily also hold for DTCS(n), that is for Pn_i=1 Φ(T^(n)_i)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and setup.

For each integer n ≥ 2, the discrete-time critical beta-splitting tree DTCS(n) is the random rooted combinatorial tree on n labeled leaves defined recursively as follows. Start from a root carrying the leaf-set {1,…,n}. A cluster of m ≥ 2 leaves is split into two child clusters of sizes i and m−i (1 ≤ i ≤ m−1) with probability
  q_m(i) = (1/h_{m−1}) · 1/(i(m−i)),  where h_{m−1} = Σ_{j=1}^{m−1} 1/j,
independently for distinct clusters, until every cluster has size 1 (a leaf). The resulting finite rooted tree, with its labeled leaves, is DTCS(n).

For a uniformly chosen leaf i ∈ {1,…,n}, let T_i^{(n)} denote the rooted plane tree obtained by re-rooting DTCS(n) at leaf i (so that T_i^{(n)} records the structure of DTCS(n) as viewed from leaf i). It is known that the local weak limit, as n → ∞, of the random sequence (T_i^{(n)}, i = 1, …, n) exists and is a stationary process (T_i, i ∈ ℤ) taking values in an appropriate space of rooted locally finite trees; call this the stationary fringe process.

Let Φ be a measurable real-valued functional on the tree-space such that Φ(T_i^{(n)}) and Φ(T_i) are well-defined.

Question.

Suppose that Φ satisfies a central limit theorem along the stationary fringe process, in the sense that there exist constants μ ∈ ℝ and σ > 0 such that
  (1/√m) · ( Σ_{i=0}^{m−1} Φ(T_i) − m μ )  ⇒  𝒩(0, σ^2)  as m → ∞.

Does it then follow that the analogous central limit theorem holds for DTCS(n), namely
  (1/√n) · ( Σ_{i=1}^{n} Φ(T_i^{(n)}) − n μ )  ⇒  𝒩(0, σ^2)  as n → ∞?

Determine whether this implication is true for every such functional Φ, or exhibit a Φ for which the fringe-process CLT holds but the DTCS(n) CLT fails.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in the overview of the critical beta-splitting random tree model. Subsequent works (2024–2025) on this model develop CLTs for specific functionals (leaf heights, harmonic descent chain, contraction methods) but do not establish a general transfer principle from fringe-process CLTs to DTCS(n) CLTs for arbitrary functionals Φ. No source located resolves the general question, so it appears to remain open.

status_evidence.snippet: New CLTs for specific functionals of the critical beta-splitting tree.
status_evidence.claim: Recent CLT progress is functional-specific and does not establish a general fringe-to-DTCS transfer.

status_evidence.title: Critical beta-splitting, via contraction
status_evidence.snippet: Contraction-method CLTs for the critical beta-splitting model.
status_evidence.claim: No general transfer principle proved; only specific CLTs.
